exercise1.prompt: Read the columns you want, and stop carrying the ones you do not.

hiddenCases.name: already tidy names are left alone

exercise1.hint: Build a dictionary from each existing name to its tidy version, then hand it to rename. str.lower() and str.replace(" ", "_") do the work.

choices: Reads only the columns you name
questions.explain: It filters on the way in, so the columns you do not want are never built at all.

choices: A new table with the new names
questions.explain: Like drop, it hands back a copy. Forgetting to reassign is why a rename can appear to do nothing.

questions.prompt: Why tidy column names at all?
choices: So every later line can use the same predictable name
questions.explain: A name with a space or a capital has to be quoted and remembered exactly. Tidying once means the rest of the analysis stops thinking about it.
